sections.content: Large codebases need systems: BEM naming, design tokens via custom properties, layered files (reset → tokens → base → components → utilities), and linting (stylelint) to enforce conventions.
CSS-in-JS and utility frameworks (Tailwind) trade hand-written CSS for generated utilities — same cascade rules apply underneath. Pick one approach and document it.
Key points: consistency beats cleverness, tokens make rebranding cheap, and dead CSS deletion is part of the job.
